title: Kvernhaug Core .kbhbrew V1
description: Machine-readable Core V1 schema for a Kvernhaug brew/batch record (.kbhbrew). Normative document: docs/development/CORE_KBHBREW_V1.md. Governs the wire contract only -- App/Web local storage/UI details are out of scope (KBH_CORE_CONTRACT.md Section 1). additionalProperties is deliberately true throughout: unknown-field passthrough is a required V1 guarantee (CORE_KBHBREW_V1.md Section 5.13), so a reader/writer implementing this schema must never reject a record purely for carrying an extra field it does not recognize.

format.description: Must equal exactly "kbhbrew" -- any other value is rejected, never guessed or coerced (Section 5.2).

version.description: Envelope version. Only 1 is supported by this schema -- any other value (including a non-integer) is rejected explicitly (Section 5.2, 5.15).

exportedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of export. Not the same as brew.createdAt/brewedAt.

brew.description: The brew/batch record itself. brewId/recipeId are LOCAL identity (Section 5.3) -- a canonical exported .kbhbrew file never carries them (see the frozen legacy fixture tests/fixtures/legacy/web/kbhbrew_v1.json), but a full local-storage record (Web's kvernhaug_web_brygg item shape) may. Both are therefore optional here, not required.

brewId.description: LOCAL storage identity only. Minted locally, never adopted from an imported file -- a reader must never treat an incoming brewId as authoritative (Section 5.3).

originBrewId.description: Portable/historical identity. Travels with an export and identifies the same real-world brewing event across machines. Defaults to brewId at creation (Section 5.3). Import dedup key (Section 5.14).

parentBrewId.description: Reserved for a future shared-batch concept. Always null in V1 -- no reader may assign meaning to a non-null value yet (Section 5.3).

recipeId.description: WEAK reference for navigation/grouping only. Display must never depend on it; the frozen snapshot is always authoritative (Section 4, 5.4). Local-machine-scoped -- never adopted from a file.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601. When the record was created -- always present (Section 5.11).

brewedAt.description: ISO 8601. The actual brew day. Optional -- may be set later than createdAt, or never (Section 5.11).

status.description: Metadata, not a state machine -- freely reassignable in any direction (Section 5.10). A discarded brew is full, valid history.

snapshot.description: Layer 2: frozen plan. Written exactly once, at brew creation, and never modified afterward (Section 5.5) -- this schema cannot itself enforce write-time immutability, that is a reader/writer behavioral rule, not a shape rule.

recipe.description: A frozen COPY of a .kbhrecipe-shaped payload (Section 5.4) -- not a live reference. Not re-validated against the .kbhrecipe schema here; that is a sibling contract's concern.

ingredientsSnapshot.description: Owner decision #1 (Option A, ratified): FULL embedded ingredient master-data entries for every non-custom ingredient the recipe references -- not a hand-picked subset, not an id+version reference (Section 5.5, Section 8 #1). Custom ingredients live in snapshot.recipe already and are deliberately absent here.

ingredientMap.description: Map of ingredient id -> the FULL master-data entry as it existed at snapshot time. Values are intentionally unconstrained (additionalProperties) -- the whole point of full embedding is that the snapshot does not have to know in advance which fields a future calculation might need (Section 8 #1's rejection of the hand-picked-subset Option C).

predicted.description: Frozen prediction snapshot (og/fg/abv/ibu/ebc/buGu/flavorProfile/style). This abv is the PREDICTED value from the calculation engine, distinct from -- and not to be confused with -- the actual-ABV wire ban in #/$defs/actuals (Section 5.7, Owner decision #3).

style.description: Reduced to {stil, score} -- localized balanse/problemer/mangler text is deliberately NOT frozen (Section 2).

provenance.description: Section 5.12. engineVersion/recipeSchemaVersion/capturedAt are the stable core. `datasets` is the normative Core-manifest-derived target (schema_version/data_version/checksum per referenced dataset, matching core/manifest.json -- CORE_VERSIONING.md); `masterdata` (entry-count proxy) is the legacy/de-facto shape Web has produced historically and remains READABLE, not the V1 target (Section 5.12, Section 6). A writer is not required to populate `datasets` if it has no trustworthy way to obtain manifest values (see the documented Web publication gap, Section 5.12/Section 8 #1 closing note) -- but must never fabricate one.

datasets.description: Normative Core manifest provenance target, keyed by dataset name (malt/humle/gjaer).

masterdata.description: Legacy/de-facto Web provenance proxy (entry counts only). Remains valid, readable data on brews already captured under it -- not the V1 normative target (Section 5.12).

datasetProvenance.description: Per-dataset Core manifest reference, matching core/manifest.json's per-dataset shape (CORE_VERSIONING.md).

actuals.description: Layer 3: sparse instrument measurements. Every field optional and independently nullable/omittable (Section 5.6). Deliberately does NOT define a derived actual-ABV field (og/fg-derived) or an actual-process-used field as canonical V1 properties -- Owner decisions #3 (Option A: omit from wire entirely) and #5 (Option B: defer) (Section 5.7). additionalProperties stays true for genuine forward-compatible passthrough of a FUTURE field -- it does not retroactively make either of those two a canonical V1 field.

og.description: Specific gravity as a plain decimal, e.g. 1.053 -- never SG points (Section 5.6).

sensing.description: Layer 4: the brewer's subjective, documented experience -- distinct from actuals (Section 5.8).

learning.description: Layer 5: forward-looking payload for the next brew of the same recipe (Section 5.9).

nextTime.description: The single most important value in the model -- surfaced before a new brew starts (Section 5.9).
